title: Observer and Strategy
idea: Observer lets one object announce events to any number of subscribers; Strategy lets an object swap the algorithm behind one method at runtime.

analogy.text: A newsletter: readers sign up, and every issue reaches them all (Observer). The editor picks a printer, local or online, without rewriting the issue (Strategy).
analogy.breaks: Code observers run one by one, inside the publisher's call.

points: The subject is the object observers subscribe to; it calls each on publish.
Subscribing returns an unsubscribe handle, so an observer can leave cleanly.
A strategy is an object with one agreed method, such as `cost(parcel)`.
The context is the object holding a strategy; swapping it changes behaviour, not code.

steps.caption: Three observers call `subscribe` on `OrderEvents`. The subject stores them and knows nothing else about them.
Checkout publishes one order. It talks only to the subject, never to the observers.
The subject calls every observer in turn, each with the same order.
Shipping prices the order by delegating to its current strategy, `FlatRate`.
Swap the strategy to `ByWeight`. Neither the subject nor the observer code changes.
Stock calls its unsubscribe handle. The next order reaches only the observers that remain.

code.title: Observer
code.caption: Add a third subscriber that logs the order id, then run it again.

walk.text: A private `Set` holds the listeners. The same function added twice is stored once.
`subscribe` stores the function and returns another function that removes it.
`publish` calls every listener with the same data, in subscription order.
Two observers react to one event. Neither knows the other exists.
After `stop()`, only the email listener runs for order 8.

code.title: Strategy
code.caption: Write an `Express` strategy that doubles the flat rate, and pass it to `setStrategy`.

walk.text: Three strategies share one method, `cost(parcel)`. That shared shape is the interface.
`Shipping` holds one strategy, set in the constructor and replaceable later.
`quote` delegates. No `if` on the strategy type appears anywhere.
One context, three behaviours, chosen while the program runs.

pitfalls: Unsubscribe observers you no longer need, or they keep firing and leak memory.
A throwing observer stops later ones in a synchronous loop; catch errors inside each.
Skip Strategy when two fixed branches will never grow; a plain `if` reads better.

quiz.why: Both listeners run for `emit(1)`. Calling `off()` removes B from the list, so `emit(2)` reaches only A.

takeaway: Observer decouples who reacts; Strategy decouples how the work gets done.

starters: How is Observer different from Node's EventEmitter?
When is Strategy better than passing a plain function?
